clue.text: One not believing in acting, so sorry

indicators.note: sorry in the sense of being in a sorry state, so these letters are knocked out of shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor confesses to performing so badly that they apologise for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorry' rearranges ACTINGSO; 'in' is only a link between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who neither believes nor disbelieves in God, holding it unknowable, is a doubter rather than a believer.

clue.text: Meagre quality of girl wearing not so much

indicators.note: the girl is worn inside the other word, which wraps around her like clothing

parts.note: not so much means less
Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl in skimpy clothing looks undernourished.
explanation.definitionFit: Being thin or scanty, with no fat or abundance, is a synonym for meagreness.

clue.text: Fish has got left stored — in fridge perhaps?

indicators.note: the letter is stored away inside the fish, as food is kept in a cupboard

parts.note: the cod is a fish

explanation.surface: Someone notices a fish has been left in the fridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has got' is a link; the definition describes the condition of things kept in a fridge, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Food kept in a fridge is chilly, an example of the temperature state, signalled by the question mark.

clue.text: Archbishop's capital line

definitions.meaning: in some churches an archbishop presiding over a province is styled by a title meaning belonging to a mother city, so the word describes what is the archbishop's
a London Underground line named after the capital city itself

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an archbishop of a province and one of the lines on the London Underground.

clue.text: Carried round a large island

parts.note: borne is a past participle of bear, meaning carried
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Something was transported around a big island.
explanation.definitionFit: Shared by Indonesia, Malaysia and Brunei, it is the third-largest island in the world.

clue.text: Mrs Simpson, captivating old princess, recalled graphic character

indicators.note: recalled read as called back, so the whole assembly is read from end to start
captivating means holding captive, so one piece is held within the other

parts.note: Marge is Mrs Simpson in the cartoon The Simpsons
Di was the familiar name of Diana, Princess of Wales

explanation.surface: A story about Wallis Simpson charming a princess, remembered in a picture.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Simpson suggests Wallis Simpson, but here it is the cartoon wife. 'captivating' holds the old inside her name, the princess follows, and 'recalled' turns everything round.
explanation.definitionFit: A written symbol representing an idea rather than a sound, as in Chinese script, is a graphic character.

clue.text: Monsieur blocking "bishop takes bishop" prior to a general cycle

indicators.note: prior to means coming before, so this piece precedes the general
the abbreviation blocks the gap between the two bishops by sitting between them

parts.note: in chess notation a bishop capturing a bishop is written B x B
Ike was the nickname of General Dwight D. Eisenhower

explanation.surface: A Frenchman interrupts a chess move before a military commander rides off on his bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: In chess notation x means 'takes', so B x B gives BXB.
explanation.definitionFit: A bicycle built for stunts and off-road racing is a kind of cycle.

clue.text: Hollow king, say, a brutal one

parts.note: a cave is a hollow in rock
a king is an example of a chessman, or man, on the board

explanation.surface: A monarch is described as hollow and cruel.
explanation.definitionFit: A prehistoric cave dweller is used figuratively for a crude, brutish fellow.

clue.text: Tries hanging around virgin, off and on

indicators.note: the wall covering goes around the letters taken from the second word

parts.note: an arras is a tapestry wall hanging

indicators.note: take letters alternately, skipping one and keeping the next

explanation.surface: Someone is tried for hanging about near a virgin, intermittently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hanging' looks like an execution but is a tapestry; 'off and on' keeps the even letters of virgin, which the tapestry goes 'around'.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring someone before a court to answer a charge is to try them, as a synonym.

clue.text: Heartless funding groups making tracks

indicators.note: heartless means losing the heart, so the central letters of the word are taken out

parts.note: sponsors are bodies that fund events

explanation.surface: Uncaring backers create a trail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' removes NS, the two middle letters of SPONSORS; 'making' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoor is the trail of an animal, its tracks or droppings.

clue.text: Capital generated by iron ore and jade I carved

indicators.note: carved means cut into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A city built from iron ore and jade carved by hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carved' rearranges IRONORE plus JADEI; 'generated by' and 'and' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: This Brazilian city was the capital of Brazil until 1960, and is a state capital still.

clue.text: One short term for Cambridge, possibly student's last

parts.note: Cambridge is an example of a university, shortened to uni

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A student's final short term at Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A single thing or quantity of one is a unit, a synonym.

clue.text: Cast angry regard

parts.note: cross means angry
to eye something is to regard it

explanation.surface: Someone casts a furious look.
explanation.definitionFit: A cast in the eye is a squint, a condition in which the eyes turn inward.

clue.text: Has droog beaten up troublemakers in estates?

indicators.note: beaten up means knocked about, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A droog from A Clockwork Orange beats up troublemakers on housing estates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beaten up' rearranges HASDROOG. Estates looks like housing estates; in Britain an estate is also an estate car, a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: Inconsiderate drivers, here pictured in estate cars, are menaces on the road, a playful definition.

clue.text: Two wives run apart in darkness to find something luminous

indicators.note: apart says the run goes in separately from the wives, at a different place in the darkness
in places the wives inside the darkness word

parts.note: gloom is darkness
W is the abbreviation for wife, twice
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Two wives run off separately into the dark to find a glowing thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apart' matters: the wives and the run do not go in together but at separate points of the darkness word.
explanation.definitionFit: A beetle whose female gives off light is a luminous creature.

clue.text: Husband, small and imperial, maybe a climber

parts.note: old man is slang for husband
an imperial is a small pointed beard below the lower lip

explanation.surface: A husband is small and has an imperial manner, and perhaps climbs mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: An imperial is a tuft of beard, named after Napoleon III; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild clematis, a climbing plant with feathery seed heads, goes by this name.

clue.text: Somehow communicate with reserve, exactly as planned

parts.note: to text is one way to communicate
to book is to reserve

explanation.surface: Someone manages to communicate while holding back, entirely according to plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done by the book, a model example, is called a textbook case, an idiom.

clue.text: Caught with stolen goods: that is the devil!

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
loot is stolen goods

explanation.surface: A thief caught with the stolen goods exclaims in dismay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the pieces; clootie is a Scots name for Satan.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Clootie is a Scottish nickname for Satan, from cloot, a cloven hoof.

clue.text: Release of men held up in enclosure

indicators.note: in places the turned piece inside the fence word

parts.note: a pale is a fenced enclosure

indicators.note: held up in a down clue means lifted, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: OR, other ranks, is military shorthand for men

explanation.surface: Men held up inside a compound are freed.
explanation.definitionFit: Early conditional freedom of a prisoner is a form of release.

clue.text: Weight of explosive, on paper

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: HE is high explosive
the FT is the Financial Times newspaper

explanation.surface: How much an explosive weighs, written down on paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Heft is heaviness or weight, a synonym.

clue.text: Body of craftsmen call round together

indicators.note: the body of a word is all but its ends, so the outer letters are dropped

parts.note: masons are craftsmen in stone

indicators.note: round means turned around, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to name is to call

explanation.surface: A guild of craftsmen calls round in a group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Body of' looks like a group of craftsmen, but trims their name to its inside letters; 'round' turns the word for call backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in unison, everyone united, is an idiom meaning together.

clue.text: I belong, unexpectedly, on top of coarse Northern English peak

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second
unexpectedly suggests things turning out differently, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: rough means coarse

explanation.surface: Someone surprisingly feels they belong on a rough northern summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpectedly' rearranges IBELONG into INGLEBO. The peak is in the Yorkshire Dales.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the Yorkshire Three Peaks, this is a mountain in northern England.

clue.text: In London, face annual blues event

definitions.meaning: in Cockney rhyming slang, spoken in London, face rhymes with the slang term
a yearly rowing contest between Oxford and Cambridge, whose sportsmen are called blues

explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang swaps a word for a phrase that rhymes with it. Oxford and Cambridge athletes are 'blues' (dark and light blue).
explanation.definitionFit: It is both rhyming slang for face and the yearly Oxford against Cambridge rowing race.

clue.text: Coordinate classics baccalaureate that's partly rejected

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the run of letters is read in reverse
only part of the words is used, a run of consecutive letters inside them

explanation.surface: A school qualification in classics is partly turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partly' takes ASSICSBA from clASSICS BAccalaureate and 'rejected' turns it round; 'that's' links.
explanation.definitionFit: In graphs, the x-coordinate measured along the horizontal axis has this mathematical name.

clue.text: OK with getting mature bird to go inside

indicators.note: the bird is told to go inside the other word

parts.note: aging, a variant spelling of ageing, means getting mature
a ree is a female ruff, a wading bird

explanation.surface: Someone accepts a mature bird being brought indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: A ree, also reeve, is a female ruff; the spelling without the E of ageing is needed for the count.
explanation.definitionFit: Being OK with something means consenting to it, so the phrase is a synonym.

clue.text: Split answer getting communist union backing

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so both pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: red is a familiar term for a communist
the NUS is the National Union of Students

explanation.surface: An answer divides a communist union going backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns REDNUS into SUNDER; 'getting' links. The NUS is Britain's National Union of Students.
explanation.definitionFit: Torn into pieces, apart, describes something split.

clue.text: Privates, ultimately restless, come to dance from the south

indicators.note: in a down clue reading from the south means from bottom to top, so the whole is reversed
the last letter of each of these words is taken

parts.note: a jig is a dance

explanation.surface: Restless soldiers finally come to a dance in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives SEO from restlesS comE tO; JIG follows and 'from the south' turns SEOJIG upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: American enlisted soldiers are called by this slang name, the lowest rank being private.

clue.text: Instrument that's not broken, with odd bits missing

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are dropped, keeping the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: An instrument that has survived unharmed, though some odd parts are gone.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the odd letters of nOt BrOkEn to leave the even ones; 'that's' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A double-reed woodwind is a musical instrument.
